# Power station size for a fridge during an outage

**For a typical full-size fridge, get about 1,000-1,500 Wh for 12-24 hours, or about 2,000 Wh or more for a day-plus. It also needs a surge rating of at least ~1,300 W and a pure sine wave inverter.** Check three things:

1. **Surge watts (the most common failure).** The compressor spikes at startup, roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. Look for a surge rating of at least 1,200-1,300 W ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [BlackBoxSupplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)). A station with lots of battery but a low surge rating can still trip when the compressor starts ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
2. **Continuous watts.** Most full-size fridges run at about 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers this ([BlackBoxSupplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
3. **Watt-hours.** The compressor cycles on only about 30-40% of the time, so average use is far below the running watts. The sources estimate:
   - **~1,000 Wh:** about 16-17 hours.
   - **~1,400 Wh:** a full 24 hours, including inverter losses and headroom.
   - **~2,800 Wh:** about 2 days.

**Size it to your own fridge.** Take the kWh/year from the yellow EnergyGuide label and compute: kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = average watts. Then multiply by 24 hours per day of outage, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add ~20% headroom ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use about twice the ENERGY STAR average, and hot kitchens and frequent door openings add more. Keeping the door shut helps a lot.

## Options that fit
- **Bluetti AC180 (~1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak)** suits roughly a day with a closed door. Listed at about $399-699 ([guide and price link](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak, pure sine wave)** gives more reserve and room for a few other essentials. Listed at $699.99 after coupon ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)).
- **Bluetti AC200L (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable to 8,192 Wh)** is a good choice if you may want more capacity later. The store price is $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF ([Dealectric, affiliate link](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l)). HomeGrid HQ estimates about 33 hours of runtime for a fridge.

Two cautions:
- Prices change often, so check at checkout.
- The sources' runtime figures are estimates, not guarantees.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year, how many days of outage you want to cover, and any other loads (CPAP, router, freezer), I can narrow this to a specific unit.
